correctness.rationale: For each nonempty cyclic binary row, every missed k-window lies in exactly one maximal zero gap, which contributes max(g-k+1,0) start positions; the exact sum gives the inverse tail counts and integral second differences. Every row with gaps g_1,...,g_r requires sum(g_i+1)<=n because cyclic zero runs need nonzero separators. Conversely any allocation satisfying those inequalities yields an explicit concatenated cyclic word with exactly the target gaps, including all-one empty-bin rows. Equal first differences and R_n=s force the complete target curve. In explicit unary dimensions the binary incidence matrix is a polynomial-size NP certificate; the 3-PARTITION reduction uses n=B,s=m, item sizes a_i and rational curve R_k=m-(1/B)sum(a_i-k)_+, with exact total-bin-capacity saturation, polynomial output on strong NP-hard instances, and 3-item grouping forced by B/4<a_i<B/2. The included finite checker completed direct exact-rational verification of 38,373 binary incidence matrices and representative feasible/infeasible cases, supplementing rather than replacing the unrestricted proof.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Replacing detected-species means by numbers of wholly unoccupied cyclic windows yields a zero-run transform. Its inversion is elementary but only recovers pooled run counts. Neither single-word run enumeration nor full-relation topological reconstruction implies the ecological criterion that these counts be packable into exactly s species rows, and the full decision problem is strongly NP-complete. No identified exact equivalent statement covers both inversion and cross-species feasibility. The full Ota–Manada paper was checked: it takes a single realized string as input and solves uniqueness under an automaton condition, rather than multirow existence from aggregated monochromatic substring counts.

originality.rationale: The verified structural theorem is not a mere restatement of the elementary run-count or classical bin-packing facts: it gives a complete if-and-only-if characterization of exactly which all-scale contiguous-window mean ecological richness profiles admit an s-species cyclic incidence realization and proves strong NP-completeness through an explicit, size-preserving gap-spectrum map. Full relevant forward and geometric ecological sources were materially inspected, and published-index, alias, complexity, run-count and curve-realizability searches revealed no stronger covering claim. Closely related circular-run and stochastic-SAR literature is acknowledged as a residual risk, rather than treated as proof of novelty.
residual_risks: The exact gap inversion may have been rediscovered under cyclic substring-count terminology outside the located sources; no exhaustive bibliography exists.

Full texts of the 1997 Leitner–Rosenzweig article and the 2013 Makri–Psillakis–Arapis run-counting article were not inspected; their stated abstracts are distinct but unidentified stronger results may exist.
The result does not establish novelty against unpublished ecological or combinatorial work; published semantic search and available full texts support only a bounded originality judgment.

value.rationale: Exact nested sliding-window richness profiles are natural spatial sampling summaries: ecologists seek to interpret changes in species–area curves as evidence of aggregation and occupancy (Tjørve et al. 2008), and geometric sampling design matters (Storch 2016). The theorem provides a nontrivial sharp feasibility test for the complete profile, identifies exactly which pooled zero-run statistics such measurements determine, and proves an intrinsic strong NP-completeness obstacle caused by unknown species allocation. The explicit monotone-concave but infeasible curve rules out a tempting shape-only description. It is useful as a theoretical baseline for ecological inverse inference and consistency checking, without overstating empirical noise-robustness or full spatial reconstruction.
